prompt: Build a JMenuBar of JMenus and JMenuItems, then walk that tree to count items and report the menu path of an item. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A menu bar is a small tree, and Swing gives you a typed accessor at each level: JMenuBar.getMenu(i) returns a JMenu, and JMenu.getItem(j) returns a JMenuItem. getItem can return null for a separator, so a defensive null check keeps the walk safe once real menus grow dividers. Menus are identified here by their visible text rather than by setName, which is why every lookup has to scan the bar -- factoring that scan into one private helper keeps addItem, itemCount and pathOf short. Returning -1 for a missing menu distinguishes it clearly from a menu that exists but is empty, which would be 0.
hints: Write one private helper that loops over bar.getMenuCount() and returns the JMenu whose getText() matches, or null -- then build the three public methods on top of it.
JMenu.add(new JMenuItem(text)) adds an item; JMenu.getItemCount() counts them.
pathOf needs a nested loop: the outer over the menus of the bar, the inner over the items of each menu. Return as soon as the text matches, and null only after both loops finish.
